title: [repost for editing error] Maybe my expectations were just too high! ...
transcript: Did you know that A24, the indie film studio bought an off-Broadway playhouse and renovated it to look like a movie theatre while still using it for live productions? Well, the vibes are very cool, but I have to admit the renovation is a bit of a mixed bag for me. I was excited to return to the iconic Cherry Lane Theatre for the first time in almost six years. This is actually the oldest operating off Broadway theatre in the city, which means it has a lot of charm, but at the same time, Let’s just say I wasn't disappointed to hear that this 100 year old theatre was getting a bit of an update And I have to admit, there's a fun novelty to going to see a live play and getting greeted with a slightly elevated movie theatre aesthetic from the smell of popcorn, to chairs with cup holders and even a little souvenir ticket And there's no denying that it's very sleek and classy. They even built a restaurant at the back of the lobby. Although therein might lie some of the problem. It's been a while since I've been in the theatre, but I'm pretty sure the lobby is quite a bit more cramped than it was before. With a very awkward sense of egress that crams the concession line, the bathroom line, the restaurant line, and the line to enter the theatre into virtually one small bottlenecked space. On a similar note, They only have three private bathrooms to serve the 167 audience members. And while the bathrooms themselves are very nice, The capacity feels like something you'd see *before* a renovation, not after. And yet they had room to cram a restaurant into the building? Still, I'm excited to see the future of what A24 can bring to the theatre landscape. Their grand reopening is with Weer by Natalie Palamides, which is a delightfully insane solo clown performance which pays homage to 90s RomComs where she plays two people in a couple, one with each half of her body. And it's become a big hit. It's been extended through December 21st! The theatre is still very much worth visiting, especially if the programming stays as good as Weer But like I said, some of these renovation choices felt like a missed opportunity, if not a step in the wrong direction.
